summary.en: Salvadoran special forces and 450 troops have been sent to Haiti to search for four missing Salvadoran soldiers and four kidnapped aviation technicians after a gang ambush, while President Bukele says recovered remains are not those personnel. Haitian gangs continue targeted attacks, forcing civilians to flee the communes of Petite Rivière de l'Artibonite and Arcahaie. The Dominican Republic has reinforced its southern frontier and border with Haiti amid the security crisis, while press freedom in Haiti is reported as critical. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske spesialstyrker og 450 soldater har blitt sendt til Haiti for å lete etter fire savnede salvadoranske soldater og fire kidnappede luftfartsteknikere etter et gjengangrep, mens president Bukele sier at de gjenfunnet restene ikke er disse personene. Haitiske gjenger fortsetter målrettede angrep, og tvinger sivile til å flykte fra kommunene Petite Rivière de l'Artibonite og Arcahaie. Den dominikanske republikk har forsterket sin sørlige grense og grensen mot Haiti i møte med sikkerhetskrisen, mens pressefriheten i Haiti rapporteres som kritisk. Konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
